The Jamaat–Qawmi Divide Through the Eyes of Gen Z: Who Is Reaping the Benefits?

Differences of opinion between Jamaat-e-Islami and scholars of the Qawmi madrasa tradition are hardly a new phenomenon. At times, these debates remain subdued and relatively calm; at others, they flare up with considerable intensity.

There are moments when it seems that the two sides are overcoming their mutual differences and moving towards a common understanding. Yet, shortly afterwards, the distance between them widens once again. Recently, it has almost seemed as though someone is deliberately adding fuel to the fire.

The issues over which they dispute are not new. Rather, long-standing disagreements are repeatedly resurfacing in new forms.

It is possible that the two sides will never reach complete agreement on these questions, given the fundamental differences in their intellectual orientations, perspectives, and modes of presentation.

One side tends to adhere strongly to tradition and conservative outlooks, while the other seeks to understand the demands of the times, the realities of society, and contemporary intellectual challenges—and to respond to them, sometimes through adaptation and sometimes by attempting to interpret new realities from an Islamic perspective.

Their priorities, too, differ considerably.

Regrettably, a sense of superiority and self-righteousness appears to exist, to varying degrees, on both sides. As a result, many are often reluctant to acknowledge the legitimacy or contributions of the other, sometimes descending into extreme narrow-mindedness.

Determining which side holds the more correct or realistic position is a complex matter that cannot be adequately addressed within the limited scope of this discussion.

History shows that disagreements among scholars have existed throughout the ages, continue to exist today, and will likely persist in the future. Conflicts of interest and differences in perspective are enduring features of human society.

It is therefore unrealistic to imagine that these disputes will one day disappear entirely. This does not, however, mean that remaining silent about them is the only solution. Such issues can and should be discussed, but within appropriate limits, in measured language, and through research-oriented and academic engagement.

In these circumstances, our responsibility is to keep disagreements within tolerable bounds and translate the principle of al-ittiḥād ma‘a al-ikhtilāf—unity despite differences—into practice for the greater welfare of the Ummah and the nation.

Both sides must remain vigilant to ensure that differences of opinion do not escalate into division, damaging mutual relationships, goodwill, and respect.

Forces opposed to Islam, along with secularist and liberalist groups, may seek to exploit these internal disputes to advance their political or intellectual interests, potentially turning us, indirectly, into instruments of their strategic objectives.

It is therefore incumbent upon responsible scholars, senior mentors, and thoughtful individuals on both sides to recognise the gravity of the situation, exercise appropriate influence over their followers, and take a firm stand against any further escalation of these disputes.

Otherwise, neither side will truly benefit. Instead, both will become progressively weaker. That is the likely consequence if the present course continues unchecked.

We must not forget that today's generation, particularly Gen Z, is more aware, questioning, inquisitive, and critical than previous generations in many respects. Young people no longer accept the statements of every scholar, shaykh, or pīr as unquestioningly as they may once have done. In this age of information, critical inquiry has become a natural part of their intellectual lives. They have learned to examine claims in the light of reason, evidence, and practical realities.

In such a context, any intemperate conduct, extreme position, or crude and unrefined statement on our part is likely to breed indifference and distrust towards us among younger people. This hardly needs further explanation.

We must therefore exercise greater care, restraint, and wisdom in both our words and our conduct. We must remain alert to the possibility that something we say or do may create misconceptions in the minds of young people about the nobility of Islam's ideals.

Ensuring that the new generation does not develop hostility towards Islam is a responsibility we all share.

May Allah Almighty grant us all sound understanding, discernment, and wisdom. Āmīn.
